items.statement: Among children aged 2 to 17 discharged after an asthma admission in 2022 to 2025, a complete five-section plan is associated with a lower rate of asthma emergency revisit or readmission within 90 days (adjusted hazard ratio 0.80 or lower) than an incomplete plan.
items.rationale: Need and practice change are high because a funding decision depends on it; novelty is moderate because one cohort elsewhere found an association (c1); feasibility depends on the linkage agreement.
items.risks: Residual confounding by engagement; delayed linkage; misclassification of completeness from illegible entries.

items.statement: The association is weaker for children whose caregivers prefer a language other than English.
items.rationale: Understanding of English plans is lower in this group (c4), so completeness may matter less when the plan cannot be used.
items.risks: Small subgroup and wide intervals; language preference may be missing from older charts.

items.statement: Completeness of the yellow-zone section alone accounts for most of any association.
items.rationale: The yellow zone is the section most often missing and hardest to score (c3).
items.risks: Item-level analyses multiply comparisons and are prone to chance findings.

summary: Three hypotheses; h1 selected as the single primary comparison, with h2 as a pre-specified equity analysis.
